question: Art collector Heinz Berggruen bought hundreds of works. Why did his collection become so valuable?
options: A handful soared and outweighed the rest
Every work rose steadily in value
He only ever bought famous pieces
answer: Because a few works, Picassos, Klees, Matisses, became immensely valuable and paid for all the ones that went nowhere. Housel calls it 'tails, you win': in investing, business and careers, a small number of events drive most results, so you can be wrong often and still do very well.
move: A few big wins can outweigh many small losses.
trap: 'Every work rose': we imagine good collectors pick only winners.
simply: If you plant twenty seeds and only two grow into huge trees, those two can still give you more fruit than a whole garden of small plants.
why: It makes failures easier to bear: in many fields, the goal is not to avoid every miss but to stay in the game long enough to catch the few big hits.
source: Morgan Housel, The Psychology of Money, 2020
reference: Morgan Housel, The Psychology of Money (Harriman House, 2020), ch. 6
